R0211.title: Smart Home Privacy Eavesdropping
R0211.definition: Smart speakers, cameras and other home devices are remotely controlled by attackers to eavesdrop on user voice, video and other private information.

references.title: Data breaches are a reality: smart-home privacy risks
FTC Securing Your Internet-Connected Devices at Home

R0211.description:
Smart home privacy eavesdropping occurs when cameras, doorbells, speakers, TVs, or hubs are accessed or controlled without authorization. Attackers can capture audio, video, routines, and household details.

Home devices often ship with weak defaults, cloud account weaknesses, or long patch gaps. Vendors need secure defaults, cloud access control, anomaly alerts, and firmware update support.
R0211.influence: Compromised smart home devices can expose private audio, video, routines, and household information to attackers.

observables: Smart cameras or speakers use default credentials with long-unupdated firmware
Home device cloud accounts show remote logins or anomalous sessions
Device audio/video streams are abnormally pulled or forwarded to external storage
Devices keep uploading audio or video data outside usage windows
Home networks show devices persistently reaching out to unfamiliar servers
